data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological fitness is reproductive success (inductive outcome), whereas Popperian corroboration is a logical status report.","Engineers use safety factors assuming material consistency (induction), whereas Popper explicitly denies consistency guarantees.","Natural selection has no conscious agent choosing; scientists actively choose theories based on methodological rules."],"overturn_conditions":["If it is shown that selecting the 'fittest' bridge inherently requires an inductive belief in material uniformity.","If biological survival is proven to be a probabilistic indicator of future survival rather than just a historical record.","If the analogy fails to account for the normative 'ought' of scientific preference versus the descriptive 'is' of natural selection."],"shared_structure":["Selection based on past performance does not guarantee future survival.","Preference is given to the entity that has survived the most severe stress tests.","The goal is not to predict immortality but to identify the most robust candidate for the next challenge.","Past survival indicates high resistance to specific known threats, not general invulnerability."],"source_memory_refs":["SURVIVAL_OF_THE_FITTEST_BIOLOGY","BRIDGE_ENGINEERING_SAFETY_FACTORS"],"transfer_claims":["Just as engineers test bridges to failure to find the strongest design without guaranteeing it will never fall, scientists test theories to find the most corroborated without guaranteeing truth.","Survival of the fittest describes a historical fact, not a prophecy; similarly, corroboration reports history, not probability."]},"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms not as an inductive inference that the theory is more probable, but as a methodological rule to maximize the potential for future falsification (error elimination), accepting the cost that this preference offers no rational guarantee of predictive success and treats scientific progress as a non-cumulative series of conjectures rather than an approach to certain truth.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is interpreted as increasing the logical probability of the theory being true.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the preference relies on the assumption that nature is uniform (the principle of induction).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the choice of theory is based on psychological comfort or pragmatic utility rather than testability.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mechanism claims to guarantee that the preferred theory will survive future tests.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'probability' (logical likelihood of truth) and 'corroboration' (historical report of test severity). Preference is justified functionally: a highly corroborated theory has withstood severe tests, meaning it has high empirical content. By choosing it, scientists select the theory that offers the most precise targets for future refutation. If it fails, we learn more; if it survives, it remains the best available target. This avoids induction because it does not claim the past success predicts future truth, only that the past success identifies the theory with the highest capacity to be proven wrong, which is the engine of Popperian progress.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
